page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on external network-attached storage. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.sn2.xlarge sits primarily in the lower tiers for compute and memory operations. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the bottom 25% or bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a weak read-only performance of 324.59 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 37.94 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth achieves an average rating at 33.29 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show lower-tier performance, with single-threaded gzip compression rated in the bottom 10%. However, the processor supports AVX and AVX-512F instructions, which helps maintain average performance in Passmark CPU extended instruction tests and small-scale LLM inference tasks.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, the ecs.sn2.xlarge offers a stable resource profile for workloads that require predictable CPU access without extreme performance demands. The lack of local storage and modest 2 Gbps network baseline suggest it is best suited for moderate general-purpose workloads, such as lightweight web serving, basic application hosting, and small-scale database operations where high IOPS or massive throughput are not critical. The hardware configuration represents an entry-to-mid-level tier of dedicated resources, trading off raw computational speed for resource predictability.
